hba1c.valid_range: TRE laboratory quality-control range; commonly interpreted as percent HbA1c
hba1c.primary_metric: R2 with RMSE and Pearson correlation as secondary metrics
hba1c.why_this_matters: HbA1c is a standard marker of longer-term glycemic exposure. Diet-derived features can test whether nutrient, food-chemical, metabolomic, and pathway-aware diet representations explain glycemic variation beyond simpler diet summaries.
hba1c.caveats: Diet features should be built from food logs preceding the blood draw. Medication, diabetes status, fasting state, assay differences, and time-window alignment can strongly affect interpretation.

tg.valid_range: TRE laboratory quality-control range; typically mg/dL or mmol/L depending on source normalization
tg.primary_metric: R2 with RMSE and Pearson correlation as secondary metrics
tg.why_this_matters: Triglycerides are diet-sensitive cardiometabolic biomarkers. Comparing de novo enriched diet features, NutriMatch nutrient features, and food-card embeddings can quantify whether extra chemical/metabolomic context improves prediction.
tg.caveats: Fasting status, alcohol, recent meals, medication, and blood-draw timing may dominate short-term triglyceride variation.

ldl.valid_range: TRE laboratory quality-control range; typically mg/dL or mmol/L depending on source normalization
ldl.primary_metric: R2 with RMSE and Pearson correlation as secondary metrics
ldl.why_this_matters: LDL cholesterol is a major cardiovascular risk marker. The task tests whether enriched habitual diet representations capture lipid-related signal beyond nutrient-only baselines.
ldl.caveats: Lipid-lowering medication, genetics, fasting status, and laboratory method should be considered when interpreting model performance.

fpg.valid_range: TRE laboratory quality-control range; only use as fasting plasma glucose when fasting metadata supports it
fpg.primary_metric: R2 with RMSE and Pearson correlation as secondary metrics
fpg.why_this_matters: Glucose is a proximal glycemic phenotype. Diet-enhanced representations can be evaluated against glucose when sample timing and fasting metadata are handled carefully.
fpg.caveats: This mapping is only clinically equivalent to fasting plasma glucose when the blood draw is confirmed fasting. Otherwise label it as blood glucose rather than FPG.

glyca.primary_metric: R2 with RMSE and Pearson correlation as secondary metrics
glyca.why_this_matters: GlycA is an inflammation-related metabolic marker. It is a useful test for whether enriched diet chemistry and disease/pathway features carry inflammatory signal.
glyca.caveats: Confirm the TRE field used by Phenobench and align diet windows before measurement.

vat.primary_metric: R2 with RMSE and Pearson correlation as secondary metrics
vat.why_this_matters: VAT reflects cardiometabolic risk and long-term diet/metabolic state. It is useful for testing whether enriched diet representations capture body-composition signal.
vat.caveats: VAT is influenced by age, sex, activity, medication, and imaging protocol; diet-only models are expected to be incomplete.

meal_ppgr.clinical_name: Postprandial glucose response for individual meals
meal_ppgr.adapter_note: Needs a meal-level adapter, not a participant-level embedding artifact. Candidate starting configs: configs/meal_ppgr.synthetic.yaml and configs/meal_ppgr.cgmacros.example.yaml.
meal_ppgr.why_this_matters: This is the most direct test of whether enriched food-level features improve meal response prediction.

meal_cgm_trajectory.adapter_note: Needs confirmation of Phenobench task contract and a meal-event feature artifact with time-aligned CGM labels.
meal_cgm_trajectory.why_this_matters: Trajectory prediction can test whether chemical/metabolomic food information improves temporal glucose dynamics, not only scalar response.

diet_sleep_causal_effect.clinical_name: Dietary exposure effect on subsequent sleep
diet_sleep_causal_effect.adapter_note: Needs exposure definition, causal window, and sleep outcome contract. Candidate starting config: configs/diet_sleep_causal_effect.synthetic.yaml.
diet_sleep_causal_effect.why_this_matters: This is a good downstream use case for food cards because interpretable dietary exposures can be tested against later sleep.

post_meal_movement_priority.clinical_name: Meals where post-meal movement may be most useful
post_meal_movement_priority.adapter_note: Needs meal-level diet features, activity context, and intervention-priority label or utility definition.
post_meal_movement_priority.why_this_matters: This reframes diet enhancement as decision support rather than only biomarker prediction.

gut_shannon_diversity.adapter_note: Needs confirmation of current Phenobench gut diversity task loader and target table. Candidate starting config: configs/gut_shannon_diversity_floor.synthetic.yaml.
gut_shannon_diversity.why_this_matters: This connects enriched diet features to microbiome diversity, one of the major planned TRE outcomes.

gut_species_richness.adapter_note: Needs confirmation of current Phenobench gut richness task loader and target table.
gut_species_richness.why_this_matters: Richness complements Shannon diversity and may respond to habitual diet variety and food chemical exposures.

prediabetes_type2_diabetes.adapter_note: Needs binary or multiclass disease-status task definition and Phenobench task implementation before config generation.
prediabetes_type2_diabetes.why_this_matters: Clinically important glycemic outcomes for testing long-term diet-derived disease risk signal.

tyg.adapter_note: Can be derived from triglycerides and glucose if units/timing are harmonized; task card should define formula and exclusions.
tyg.why_this_matters: TyG is a compact insulin-resistance proxy likely relevant to nutrient and food-processing features.

waist.primary_metric: R2 with RMSE and Pearson correlation as secondary metrics
waist.why_this_matters: Waist circumference is an interpretable cardiometabolic body-size marker that can be compared with VAT and obesity outcomes.
waist.caveats: Diet-only prediction may be strongly confounded by age, sex, physical activity, and total energy balance.

waist_hip_ratio.primary_metric: R2 with RMSE and Pearson correlation as secondary metrics
waist_hip_ratio.why_this_matters: Waist-to-hip ratio captures fat distribution and is a useful adjacent metabolic outcome for habitual diet representation evaluation.
waist_hip_ratio.caveats: Anthropometric measurement protocol and confounders should be handled explicitly.

fatty_liver_liver_attenuation.clinical_name: Fatty liver status and liver attenuation
fatty_liver_liver_attenuation.adapter_note: Needs exact Phenobench task mapping. Existing adjacent tasks may include FLI/FIB tasks, but imaging liver attenuation is a separate target if available.
fatty_liver_liver_attenuation.why_this_matters: Fatty liver outcomes are mechanistically close to diet quality, triglycerides, glucose, and inflammatory pathways.

irritable_bowel_syndrome.adapter_note: Needs phenotype definition and classification task implementation before config generation.
irritable_bowel_syndrome.why_this_matters: IBS is a plausible target for food-card and microbiome-linked diet representations, but requires careful case/control definition.
